selection.method: next 10 verified actor-primary profiles after W. N. Hildebrand taxonomy correction

profiles.name: Sammie Hill
profiles.excerpt: Sammie Hill was a versatile radio actress whose surviving work ranges from hard-boiled detective drama to westerns, anthology productions and literary adaptations.
profiles.bio_html:
Sammie Hill built a substantial career in network radio, even though comparatively little personal biography survives outside the broadcasts themselves. Cast records place her repeatedly in New York and Hollywood dramatic productions during the 1940s and 1950s.

Hill appeared across crime, western and anthology series, including Gunsmoke, Broadway Is My Beat, The Adventures of Philip Marlowe and The Line Up. The breadth of those credits shows the repertory skill required to move from one new character to another without relying on a continuing star role.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Gunsmoke performances credited to Hill, six Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances, five Broadway Is My Beat episodes, four each on The Adventures of Philip Marlowe and The Line Up, and additional work on Crime Classics, Lux Radio Theatre and Richard Diamond, Private Detective.

profiles.name: Donald Morrison
profiles.excerpt: Donald Morrison was a dependable Radio Row actor whose strongest surviving GRH work is in NBC University Theater and its ambitious adaptations of major literature.
profiles.bio_html:
Donald Morrison belonged to the professional radio repertory that network producers drew on for demanding dramatic adaptations. Personal details about his life are sparse, but contemporary program records place him repeatedly in serious network drama during the 1940s and early 1950s.

NBC University Theater became the strongest surviving concentration of Morrison's work. The series adapted major novels and plays for listeners and college-credit courses, requiring supporting actors who could handle literary dialogue alongside both Hollywood stars and veteran Radio Row performers.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 28 NBC University Theater performances credited to Morrison, two each on Rocky Jordan and Screen Directors Playhouse, and additional appearances on Lux Radio Theatre, The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe, The Whistler and Words at War.

profiles.name: Joan Lorring
profiles.excerpt: Joan Lorring began in radio as the teenage star of A Date with Judy before an Oscar-nominated film career and a later return to network radio drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Joan Lorring was born Madeline Ellis in Hong Kong in 1926. After her family fled the Japanese invasion and settled in the United States, she began acting in radio under the name Dellie Ellis. In 1942 she played the title character in A Date with Judy, making radio the starting point of her professional career.

Lorring moved quickly into film and earned an Academy Award nomination for The Corn Is Green, then built a substantial Broadway and television career. Radio remained part of her work across decades, from Suspense to Theater Five and the 1970s repertory of CBS Radio Mystery Theater.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 14 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Lorring, 12 Theater Five appearances, three Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar episodes and additional work on Academy Award Theater, Barrie Craig, Inner Sanctum Mysteries and Lux Radio Theatre.

profiles.name: D. J. Thompson
profiles.excerpt: D. J. Thompson was a busy West Coast radio actress whose surviving credits are concentrated in Johnny Dollar and other major detective dramas of the 1950s.
profiles.bio_html:
D. J. Thompson belongs to the Hollywood radio repertory whose broadcast record survives more clearly than personal biography. Cast credits place her repeatedly in crime, detective and suspense productions during the 1950s.

Her strongest surviving association is with Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, where she appeared in numerous Bob Bailey-era broadcasts. She also worked on The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, The Six Shooter, Crime Classics and Richard Diamond, Private Detective, demonstrating the flexibility expected of a supporting radio actress.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 19 Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar performances credited to Thompson, four The Adventures of Philip Marlowe appearances, two The Six Shooter episodes and additional work on A Man Called X, Broadway Is My Beat, Crime Classics, Jeff Regan, Investigator and Richard Diamond, Private Detective.

profiles.name: Donovan Faust
profiles.excerpt: Donovan Faust briefly took over one of adventure radio's most famous identities as Britt Reid and the Green Hornet during Al Hodge's wartime departure.
profiles.bio_html:
A. Donovan Faust was a Detroit broadcaster and actor associated with WXYZ during the network era. In 1943, when longtime star Al Hodge entered military service, Faust became the second performer to voice Britt Reid and his masked identity, the Green Hornet.

Faust later recalled the physical demands of performing action radio without visual reference, describing how actors jogged, punched and moved at the microphone to make fight scenes sound convincing. His career later shifted toward broadcasting management, including executive work with General Electric broadcasting stations.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 50 The Green Hornet performances credited to Faust in detailed archive records. Those broadcasts document his period carrying the title role between Hodge and later Green Hornet performers.

profiles.name: Tommy Cook
profiles.excerpt: Tommy Cook began as one of radio's busiest child actors, playing Little Beaver, Alexander and Junior before later becoming a screenwriter and producer.
profiles.bio_html:
Tommy Cook was born in Duluth, Minnesota in 1930 and entered professional radio as a child. He became one of the medium's busiest juvenile performers, with contemporary profiles crediting him with hundreds of broadcasts while he was still in his early teens.

Cook played Little Beaver on Red Ryder, Alexander on Blondie and Junior on The Life of Riley, while also working in dramatic productions. His later career expanded into animation voice acting and behind-the-camera work. He helped write and produce films including Rollercoaster and Players, making writing and production genuine second branches of his professional life.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven performances each on Lux Radio Theatre and Sears Radio Theater credited to Cook, six The Great Gildersleeve appearances, five Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar episodes, three Suspense performances and additional work on A Date with Judy, Blondie and Gunsmoke.

profiles.name: Tony Roberts
profiles.excerpt: Tony Roberts brought a distinguished Broadway career and quick comic intelligence to dozens of CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances.
profiles.bio_html:
Tony Roberts was born in Manhattan in 1939 and developed into a major Broadway actor, earning Tony Award nominations and becoming a frequent collaborator with Woody Allen on stage and film. His work depended on verbal precision and timing, qualities that translated naturally to radio.

Roberts became one of the recurring New York actors used by CBS Radio Mystery Theater. Across the series he played a wide variety of leading and supporting roles, from contemporary crime stories to supernatural and historical drama, demonstrating vocal range beyond the screen persona familiar from his film work.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 35 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Roberts. The broader series record documents dozens more appearances, making radio drama a substantial part of his New York acting career rather than an occasional sideline.

profiles.name: Joan Banks
profiles.excerpt: Joan Banks, also credited under her married name Joan Lovejoy, built a long radio career in serials, crime drama and later CBS Radio Mystery Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Joan Banks was born in New York City in 1918 and developed a career across radio, stage, film and television. During her marriage to actor Frank Lovejoy she was also credited as Joan Lovejoy, the name preserved in Golden Radio Hour's source archive.

Banks worked widely in network radio, including Gang Busters, The Falcon, Suspense, This Is Your FBI and daytime serials. Decades later she returned to network drama through Theater Five and CBS Radio Mystery Theater, sometimes appearing in the same professional orbit as her husband.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 28 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited under the Joan Lovejoy name and six Theater Five appearances. Her canonical profile uses Joan Banks while retaining Joan Lovejoy as the archive source name.

profiles.name: Anne Pitoniak
profiles.excerpt: Anne Pitoniak brought a lifetime of stage experience into radio drama, becoming a recurring CBS Radio Mystery Theater performer before receiving two Tony nominations.
profiles.bio_html:
Anne Pitoniak was born in Westfield, Massachusetts in 1922 and worked as a civilian actress-technician with the USO during World War II. She later built her career in regional theatre, New York stage work, radio and television.

Pitoniak became a recurring member of CBS Radio Mystery Theater, where the New York repertory gave experienced stage actors a new microphone outlet. Her later stage career brought major recognition, including Tony Award nominations for night, Mother and Picnic.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 27 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Pitoniak, three The Chase appearances, two X Minus One episodes and an additional Crime and Peter Chambers performance. Her canonical public name is corrected from the archive spelling Ann Pitoniak to Anne Pitoniak.

profiles.name: Dusty Walker
profiles.excerpt: Dusty Walker was a recurring supporting actor on The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok, helping populate the western series with changing characters across multiple seasons.
profiles.bio_html:
Dusty Walker is one of the radio actors whose surviving professional record is concentrated in a single series rather than in extensive later biography. Cast records repeatedly place him in The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok alongside Guy Madison, Andy Devine and the program's regular western repertory.

Walker appeared as a changing supporting player rather than one fixed continuing character. That kind of repertory work was essential to a weekly western, allowing the same dependable actors to return as townsmen, outlaws, officials and other figures while the story and setting changed.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 33 The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok performances credited to Walker. Those holdings provide a substantial record of his contribution to one of radio's most durable western adventure series.
